# SK7083 — The string literal is repeated

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

One string literal is written in a file more times than dotnet_code_quality.SK7083.threshold (default 5), counting only literals at least dotnet_code_quality.SK7083.minimum_length characters long (default 5) that contain a letter.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S1192 |

## Why

The same literal in several places is the same rename waiting to be done incompletely — the argument `nameof` makes for member names, applied to keys, formats and messages. ⚠ **It takes two options, and the second is what makes it usable.** A repeat count on its own reports `", "`, `"/"` and `"true"` long before it reports anything worth extracting, so a minimum length holds the floor and a literal must also contain a letter: a repeated separator or punctuation run is not a name anybody was going to give. ⚠ The default count is 5 — a literal must be written six times in one file — and that is the conservative end of a measurement with no wrong answer. On Skala's own tree a count of 3 reports 144 literals and a count of 5 reports 64; every one of the 144 is a real repeat, and the ones the higher default drops are the HTML fragments and fixture file names nobody was going to extract. The count is the option a repository lowers rather than raises, so the shipped number is the one that leaves room to. Choosing the name is the whole of the work, so there is no fix.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
logger.LogWarning("tenant-id header missing");
// … and "tenant-id" written again in three other places in the same file
```

Write:

```csharp
const string TenantIdHeader = "tenant-id";
```

## When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. ⚠ **The minimum length and the letter test are the rule**, not decoration: without them the default count reports every separator and every one-word flag in the repository. ⚠ **A `const` initialiser is not counted** — it is the repair, and a rule that still fires after somebody did exactly what it asked is the fastest way to teach people it is noise. ⚠ **An attribute argument is not counted**: it must be a compile-time constant, so the only extraction available is a `const` the attribute then names, and the ones that actually repeat are test display names, obsolescence messages and route templates, where writing the string out at the declaration is the point. ⚠ **Counted per file, and per file deliberately.** The scope where a repeat is visible and a `const` is an obvious repair is the one a reader has open; counting per compilation would report a literal shared by two unrelated files, where the repair is a shared constant nobody has a place for and the finding points at neither site. One finding per literal, at the first occurrence — one per site would report the same decision as many times as it was made. Interpolated strings are not literals and their text is not counted; neither are UTF-8 literals, which are a different expression kind. Comparison is ordinal on the literal's value, so a verbatim and a regular spelling of the same text count together. Generated code is excluded.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_code_quality.SK7083.threshold`
- `dotnet_code_quality.SK7083.minimum_length`
- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7083.severity`
